headline: City Council adopted the 2026 Housing Compass Plan after amending wording from 'accept' to 'adopt,' vote 7-0.
summary: The City Council and Planning Board held a joint public hearing on the 2026 Housing Compass Plan, a housing policy guide. After public comment and councilor questions, the Planning Board voted to adopt the plan, and the City Council amended and then adopted the plan as well.
decisions: The Planning Board voted to adopt the 2026 Housing Compass Plan, 7 in favor, 0 opposed.
The Planning & Development Committee recommended that the City Council accept the draft Housing Compass Plan, 2 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 absent.
The City Council voted to amend the motion by striking 'accept' and inserting 'adopt,' 7 in favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent.
The City Council voted to adopt the draft Housing Compass Plan as amended, 7 in favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent.

decision_evidence.quote: the Planning Board voted by ROLL CALL 7 in favor, 0 opposed, to adopt the 2026 Housing Compass Plan.

the Planning & Development Committee voted 2 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 absent to recommend that the City Council accept the draft Housing Compass Plan as submitted by the Community Development Director and presented on September 2, 2026.
the City Council voted 7 in favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent, to strike the word "accept" and insert the word "adopt."
the City Council voted 7 in favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent, to adopt the draft Housing Compass Plan as submitted by the Community Development Director and presented on September 2, 2026.

City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 1 of 11
GLOUCESTER CITY COUNCIL
&
PLANNING BOARD SPECIAL MEETING
Tuesday, September 29, 2026 – 6:30 p.m.
Gloucester City Hall - Kyrouz Auditorium
9 Dale Avenue, Gloucester, MA  01930
and
Remotely via Zoom
-Minutes-
Councilors Present: Council President, Councilor Tony Gross; Councilor Scott Memhard; Councilor
Hannah Kimberley; Councilor Jason Grow; Councilor Francesco Margiotta; Councilor Dylan Benson;
Councilor Marjorie Grace
Absent: Council Vice President, Councilor Sean Nolan; Councilor Patti-Ann Page
Planning Board Present: Chair, Rick Noonan; Vice Chair, Jane Remsen; David Rosen; Beverly Bookin; 
Steve Yost; Douglas Cook (remote); Shawn Henry (remote)
Also Present: Mayor Paul Lundberg; CAO Kelly Dolan (remote); City Clerk, Grace Poirier; Community
Development Director, Alex Koppelman; State Representative, Dru Tarr
This meeting was conducted with the City Council in person
and the public participating in person and remotely via Zoom.
Meeting called to order at 6:30 p.m.
Councilor Gross stated the following:
“This public meeting of the City Council is recorded on zoom with a link that is posted on the agenda. If you
are calling in on a phone, you can press Star 9 to request to speak. If you are watching on a computer or device,
there is a “raised hand” button that you can tap or press to request to speak. Please use either of these options
during oral communications and public hearings to be recognized to speak.
If technical difficulties arise and the Zoom link is interrupted during an in-person hybrid meeting of the City
Council and a quorum is present, the meeting may continue after efforts have been made to reestablish the link.
The minutes shall note the interruption.
It is the finding of the City of Gloucester that no individual should be denied equal treatment or opportunity
because of their age, ancestry, color, disability, including intellectual and developmental mental disability,
family status, immigration status, gender identity or expression, military status, marital status, national origin,
race, religion, sex or sexual orientation.”
FLAG SALUTE AND MOMENT OF SILENCE: Councilor Margiotta led the flag salute.
SCHEDULED PUBLIC HEARINGS:
1. PH2026-023: Consideration of the 2026 Housing Compass Plan
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 2 of 11
•City Council Public Hearing Opened: 6:34 p.m.
•Planning Board Public Hearing Opened: 6:34 p.m.
•Speaking in Favor: Community Development Director, Alex Koppelman shared his screen.
Alex Koppelman stated that the Housing Compass Plan was a proactive approach to the City’s housing needs
and it was written to State standards. 
Alex Koppelman stated the above. He stated that if approved by the State it would give the City greater control
over local housing.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 3 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated the above were the members of the Plan Advisory Committee.
Alex Koppelman stated the above.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 4 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated the above. He stated that there was a mismatch between housing needs and what was
available in the housing stock. He stated that there was a lack of affordable options, which led to local workers
not being able to afford to live in the City, which created traffic, and made for a weaker local economy.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 5 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated that the Housing Compass Plan had been created with a heavy emphasis on community
engagement.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 6 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated the above.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 7 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated the above.
Alex Koppelman stated the above was a map of the development constraints within the City.
Alex Koppelman stated the above. He stated that while neighborhoods outside of Downtown could not support
large scale developments due to infrastructure, they could support smaller scale development such as ADUs.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 8 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated the above were possible areas of development. He stated that these were privately owned,
but the City could encourage development in a number of ways. 
Alex Koppelman stated the above. He stated that Smart Growth Overlay District’s worked best when they were
designed with a development partner. He stated that any incentive payments from the State would go into the
City’s General Fund.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 9 of 11
Alex Koppelman stated the Housing Compass Plan was a roadmap for the City and was not binding. He stated
that any implementation of recommendations would require a public process. 
Mayor Paul Lundberg stated his support for the Housing Compass Plan.
Laura Bacchia, 10 Dale Avenue, stated her support for the matter. She stated her concerns for a grocery store
being included in any redevelopment of the former Shaw’s building on Railroad Avenue.
Deanna Fay, 3 Barberry Lane, stated she was the Chair of the Affordable Housing Trust. She stated that the
Affordable Housing Trust had voted to support the Housing Compass Plan. She stated that the Housing Compass
Plan identified the Affordable Housing Trust as a key partner in its strategies, which was appropriate. She stated
the Affordable Housing Trust was meant to be a flexible municipal resource to help create affordable housing in
the City. 
Deborah Frontierro, 216 Washington Street, stated her support for the matter. She stated that the plan was
very detailed and specific. 
Henry Harrison, 49 Sumner Street, stated he was a High School senior and that he and his peers had a hard
time staying in the City due to housing costs. He stated he supported the matter. 
Barnaby Prendergast, 61 Fernald Street, stated his support for the matter.
Valarie Nelson, 7 Sunset Point Road, stated her support for the matter. She stated that the cost of ADUs was
prohibitive and the City should look into incentives for modular or manufactured housing.
Peggy Hegarty-Steck, CEO Action Inc., 180 Main Street, stated she had been part of the advisory committee.
She stated her support for the matter. She stated through Action Inc’s own studies, the cost of housing was one of
the main concerns across all groups. 
Nick Fay, 33 Emerson Avenue, stated his support for the matter.
•Speaking in Opposition: Jane Fox, no address given, stated that the current plan did not include a fiscal impact
analysis, or how increased housing would affect the tax levy. She stated that the plan did not contain an
infrastructure capacity assessment and the City had aging infrastructure. She stated that the plan did not include
a school enrollment model, and if new housing would put a strain on the schools. She stated that the plan did not
address short term rentals. She stated that the plan did not include estimates for the cost of funding programs, and
without funding the recommendations were not actionable. She stated that the plan should be revised to address
these concerns.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 10 of 11
Beverly Palmacci, 8 Commonwealth Avenue, stated her opposition regarding the matter. She stated that
Downtown had already been rezoned and should not be further developed. 
•Communications: None.
•Questions from Councilors to Applicants/Staff: Planning Board Member David Rosen asked how long
would the Housing Compass Plan be good for. Alex Koppelman stated that the State considered it good for five
years. 
Councilor Benson asked for clarification regarding what a Gateway City designation was. Alex Koppelman
stated a Gateway City was a State designation for grant giving. He stated that the designation was for
municipalities that had a decline in industry, and had criteria based on population size and income. He stated that
the City met all the criteria except for population size, which was 5,000 below the threshold.  
Councilor Grow asked for clarification as to what priorities the City Council should set regarding the Housing
Compass Plan. Alex Koppelman stated that the City needed to continue robust community engagement. He stated
that the financing related recommendations were already being evaluated by the Affordable Housing Trust. He
stated the Housing Subcommittee of the Planning Board was also looking at zoning recommendations. He stated
that the creation of smart growth districts would also be a benefit to the City. 
Councilor Kimberly asked how much affordable housing would have local preference. Alex Koppelman stated
that when affordable housing was created then the City could request up to 70% of units have local preference,
which could include veterans and seniors. 
Councilor Benson asked for clarification on the 40Y Starter Home zoning. Alex Koppelman stated that the
Housing Subcommittee was already looking at cleaning up the cluster zoning which would be a good starting
point. He stated that there were areas within the City where such zoning would be appropriate considering the
infrastructure. 
Councilor Grace asked if the grants that were being cited as funding sources within the Housing Compass Plan
were in danger of changing in the future due to shifts in the Federal government. Alex Koppelman stated that
they were currently safe and funded through the State.
Councilor Gross asked for clarification on the 40R zoning and its relation to a grocery store downtown. Alex
Koppelman stated that in the 40R zoning the City could make a list of allowable uses. He stated that whoever
developed the project would also have to work with the City. 
Councilor Gross asked if the City needed to be concerned regarding adding conserved land and reducing the
amount of developable land. Alex Koppelman stated that conservation and development were in conflict and it
would be up to policy makers to make those decisions. 
Councilor Benson asked if there were possible funding sources for critical infrastructure such as sewer. Alex
Koppelman stated that the State had several programs to fund infrastructure, but it would require an affordable
housing development to be proposed to apply for that funding. 
Planning Board Member Shawn Henry stated that the Housing Compass Plan addresses the tension between
conservation of land and development in the section regarding right size development. 
Councilor Margiotta asked if financial concerns had been considered by the administration considering rising
costs. Alex Koppelman stated that the DPW and the Board of Health had been consulted and it had been
determined that with the upgrade to the wastewater treatment plant Downtown had the ability to be further
developed.
City Council                                         September 29, 2026                                                  Page 11 of 11
Councilor Margiotta asked if there was a deadline for the Housing Compass Plan to be submitted to the State.
Alex Koppelman stated that there was no deadline, but with an approved plan the City would have more control
over Chapter 40B applications. 
Councilor Gross asked who the City needed to lobby to create a task force to examine building codes within the
State and improve them. Alex Koppelman stated that the State should create a panel of experts.
•City Council Public Hearing Closed: 7:47 p.m.
•Planning Board Public Hearing Closed: 7:47 p.m.
PLANNING BOARD RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Jane Remsen, seconded by Steve Yost, the
Planning Board voted by ROLL CALL 7 in favor, 0 opposed, to adopt the 2026 Housing Compass Plan.
COMMITTEE RECOMMENDATION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Kimberley,
the Planning & Development Committee voted 2 in favor, 0 opposed, 1 absent to recommend that the City
Council accept the draft Housing Compass Plan as submitted by the Community Development Director and
presented on September 2, 2026.
Summary of Discussion: Councilor Gross proposed an amendment.
MOTION: A motion was made by Councilor Grow, seconded to Councilor Kimberley, to accept the draft
Housing Compass Plan as submitted by the Community Development Director and presented on
September 2, 2026.
MOTION TO AMEND: On a motion by Councilor Gross, seconded by Councilor Memhard, the City
Council voted 7 in favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent, to strike the word “accept” and insert the word “adopt.”
Summary of Discussion: Councilor Grow stated his support for the matter.
Councilor Benson stated his support for the matter.
Councilor Gross stated his support for the matter.
MOTION AS AMENDED: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Kimberley, the City
Council voted 7 in favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent, to adopt the draft Housing Compass Plan as submitted by
the Community Development Director and presented on September 2, 2026.
MOTION: On a motion by David Rosen, seconded by Jane Remsen, the Planning Board voted by ROLL
CALL 7 in favor, 0 opposed, to adjourn the meeting at 7:56 p.m.
MOTION: On a motion by Councilor Grow, seconded by Councilor Benson, the City Council voted 7 in
favor, 0 opposed, 2 absent, to adjourn the meeting at 7:57 p.m.
Submitted by: Lynds Jones, Legislative Aide
Items submitted at the meeting: None.
